reflection_question: Without softening it, name the thing you keep going back to. What does it promise you right before you reach for it?
devotional_text:
You already know why you opened this.

You do not need a definition of addiction. You do not need statistics.

You need somebody to say the true thing out loud.

So here it is.

**Something has you.**

Not "you have a bad habit." Not "you are going through a season."

Something has you, and you have tried to get free of it more than once, and you are still here.

That is not a comfortable sentence. It is an honest one. And nothing in the next sixty days works without it.

# You Are Not The First

There is a man in the Bible who wrote down exactly what this feels like.

Not a addict in the way we use the word. A man who loved God, who knew the Scriptures better than almost anyone alive, and who still could not win the fight going on inside him.

His name was Paul. He wrote this:

> "For I don't know what I am doing. For I don't practice what I desire to do; but what I hate, that I do." (Romans 7:15)

Read that again slowly.

**What I hate, that I do.**

Not what I enjoy. Not what I am proud of.

What I hate.

That is the part nobody on the outside understands. They think you must like it. They think if you really wanted to stop, you would stop.

They have never been in the room at two in the morning with the thing they swore they were finished with.

Paul had. And he put it in the Bible.

## He Goes Further

> "For the good which I desire, I don't do; but the evil which I don't desire, that I practice." (Romans 7:19)

The word there is *practice*. Not slipped. Not stumbled.

Practice. Something you do over and over until you get good at it.

That is what makes this different from a mistake. A mistake happens once. This has a rhythm to it. It has a time of day. It has a trigger. It probably has a hiding place.

## And Then He Says The Thing

> "What a wretched man I am! Who will deliver me out of the body of this death?" (Romans 7:24)

That is not a theology lesson. That is a man on the floor.

And I want you to notice what he does not say.

He does not say "who will teach me to try harder."

He does not say "who will give me a better system."

He says **who will deliver me**. Who will come and get me out.

Because by the time you are writing a sentence like that, you already know your own effort is not going to be enough. You have run that experiment. Many times.

## The Next Verse Is Why You Are Here

> "I thank God through Jesus Christ, our Lord!" (Romans 7:25)

That is the whole reason this study exists.

There is an answer to the question. It is not a technique and it is not your own willpower dressed up in church clothes.

It is a person.

And over the next sixty days we are going to walk very slowly toward Him, starting from exactly where you are and not from where you think you should be.

## Something That Has To Be Said On Day One

This is a Bible study. It is not medical care.

It is not detox, it is not therapy, it is not medication, and it is not a substitute for any of them.

If you are physically dependent on alcohol or on a drug, stopping suddenly on your own can be dangerous and in some cases deadly. Talk to a doctor.

If you are thinking about ending your life, please contact your local emergency services or a crisis line today, before you read anything else here.

**Getting help from a doctor, a counsellor or a recovery group is not weak faith.** For an enormous number of people it is the exact thing God uses. Needing other people is not a failure. It is how He built us.

## What To Watch For In Romans 7:15-25

* ⚔️ How many times Paul describes the same fight in different words
* 🪞 The difference between what he wants and what he does
* 🔗 The word "captivity" in verse 23, and why he chose a word about chains
* 😔 How honest he is willing to be before he says anything hopeful
* 🙏 Who he finally turns to in verse 25

Do not rush to the hopeful verse. Sit in the honest ones first. He did.

## The Bigger Takeaway

The fight inside you is not proof that you are a fraud.

It is proof that there is something in you that still wants out.

A person who had completely given up would not feel torn. The tearing is the fight. The fight is the sign of life.

Paul did not write Romans 7 from a position of defeat. He wrote it from inside the struggle, and then he named the only way out.

**You are not the first person to be here, and you are not outside what God does.**

## Today's One Thing

**Say it once, plainly.**

Out loud if you can. Alone is fine. Nobody else needs to hear it today.

Say the real name of the thing. Not "my struggle." Not "my issue." The actual word.

"I am addicted to ______."

Or if that word feels wrong, this one: "______ has a hold on me and I cannot get it off."

That is it. That is the whole task for today.

You are not promising anything. You are not starting a streak. You are just stopping the pretending for ten seconds.

Everything we do for the next fifty-nine days is built on top of those ten seconds.

## Today's Prayer

God,

I am tired of pretending this is under control.

You already know what it is. You have watched every single time. There is nothing I am about to tell You that will surprise You.

So I am going to stop managing how this looks and just say it.

I cannot get free of this on my own. I have tried. I keep ending up back in the same place.

I do not know how You are going to do this. I do not even know if I believe You will.

But I am here, and that is something.

Meet me in the part of this that nobody else sees.

In Jesus' name, amen.

day_title: The First Person You Lied To
reflection_question: What is the story you tell yourself about this so that it sounds smaller than it is? Write down the exact words you use.
devotional_text:
Yesterday you said the real name of it.

If you did that, something already shifted. Not the problem. The pretending.

Today we go one layer down, to the thing that keeps the problem alive.

**Before you ever lied to anybody else about this, you lied to yourself.**

You have a sentence. Everybody does. A sentence you say in your head that makes the thing sound smaller, or later, or more reasonable than it is.

* 🕐 "Just tonight."
* 🤏 "It is not that much."
* 😤 "I have earned this."
* 🔚 "I will stop properly on Monday."
* 🧊 "I could stop whenever I wanted."
* 🙂 "Other people have it way worse."

That sentence is older than you think.

# The Oldest Conversation

Genesis 3 is the first time in the Bible that anybody talks themselves into something.

Watch how it happens, because the pattern has not changed in thousands of years.

First, a question that makes the boundary sound unreasonable.

Then a flat denial of the consequence.

Then the offer.

And then this:

> "When the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was a delight to the eyes, and that the tree was to be desired to make one wise, she took some of its fruit, and ate." (Genesis 3:6)

Notice the order. She *saw*. Then she *desired*. Then she *took*.

There was a gap between seeing and taking, and in that gap she built a case.

Good for food. Delightful. Will make me wise.

Three reasons. All of them partly true. That is what makes a good lie work.

## Your Gap

You have that gap too.

It might be ninety seconds. It might be two days. But between the first thought and the actual thing, there is a stretch of time where you argue yourself into it.

And here is what matters: **you are never more persuasive than you are in that gap.**

You will make arguments to yourself that you would laugh at coming from anybody else.

That gap is where the fight is actually lost. Not at the moment you reach for it. The moment you reach for it, the decision has already been made.

## Then Comes The Hiding

> "Their eyes were opened, and they both knew that they were naked. They sewed fig leaves together, and made coverings for themselves." (Genesis 3:7)

The first instinct after is always to cover.

You know this part well. The deleted history. The story that is almost true. The breath mint. The second phone. The receipts you handle yourself. The carefully managed version of your week that you give people when they ask how you are.

Fig leaves. That is all they are.

They do not fix anything. They just make it possible to keep going.

## And Then The Distance

> "They heard Yahweh God's voice walking in the garden in the cool of the day, and the man and his wife hid themselves from the presence of Yahweh God among the trees of the garden." (Genesis 3:8)

This is the part that costs the most.

Not the thing itself. The hiding from God that comes after it.

Because you cannot be close to somebody you are managing. And at some point most people in this fight quietly stop praying honestly. They still pray. They just stop saying the real thing.

And then they are alone with it.

## What God Does Next

Read this slowly, because it is not what you would expect.

> "Yahweh God called to the man, and said to him, 'Where are you?'" (Genesis 3:9)

God asks a question He already knows the answer to.

He is not looking for information. He is giving the man a chance to speak.

**God came into the garden. He did not wait at the gate for them to come out.**

That is who He is, on the worst day in human history, and it is who He is this morning.

## What To Watch For In Genesis 3:1-13

* ❓ The first question in verse 1, and how it twists what God actually said
* ⏳ The gap in verse 6 between seeing and taking
* 🍃 What they reach for the moment they feel exposed
* 🚶 Who moves first in verse 8, and who moves first in verse 9
* 👉 How quickly blame starts in verses 12 and 13

## The Bigger Takeaway

You did not end up here because you are stupid. You ended up here because the argument was good.

It is still good. It will be good again today.

The way out is not to become somebody who never hears it. It is to learn to recognise it while it is happening, and to stop trusting your own case.

**You are not a reliable witness about this one thing. That is not shame. That is just true, and knowing it is the beginning of beating it.**

## Today's One Thing

**Write your sentence down.**

The exact one. The words you actually use in your head.

Not a tidy version. The real one, with however it is phrased.

Put it in your phone, or on paper, or in the reflection box on this page.

Then under it write four words: *This is the lie.*

You are not trying to never think it again. You are labelling it, so that the next time it shows up you recognise the voice instead of mistaking it for your own good judgement.

Naming a thing takes some of its power. That is why God brought the animals to Adam to be named, and it is why the first thing you did in this study was say the real word.

## Today's Prayer

God,

I am good at talking myself into things.

I have built a whole case, and I have been the judge and the jury in it, and I keep returning the same verdict.

Show me the moment it starts. Not after. During.

When the argument comes and it sounds exactly like my own voice, give me enough of a pause to notice what is happening.

And God, I do not want to hide from You any more. I have been giving You the edited version.

You came looking for them in the garden. You did not wait at the edge.

Come and find me where I actually am.

In Jesus' name, amen.

reflection_question: Is there one person who could know the truth about this and not use it against you? If there is nobody, what would it take to find one?
devotional_text:
There is a particular kind of tiredness that comes from keeping a secret.

It is not the same as being busy tired. Sleep does not fix it.

It is the tiredness of running a second life in the background. Keeping the stories straight. Remembering who knows what. Managing the gap between how you look and how you are.

David wrote a song about it.

# He Describes It Physically

> "When I kept silence, my bones wasted away through my groaning all day long." (Psalm 32:3)

Bones wasting away.

He is not being poetic for the sake of it. Carrying something hidden does something to your body.

You know this. The tightness when the phone rings. The flinch when somebody opens the wrong drawer. The way your chest goes when somebody says your name in a certain tone.

> "For day and night your hand was heavy on me. My strength was sapped in the heat of summer." (Psalm 32:4)

**Sapped.** Drained out slowly.

That is where a lot of people in this fight live for years. Not dramatic. Just slowly running out.

## The Silence Is Not Protecting You

Here is the thing nobody tells you.

You think the secret is keeping you safe. That is the deal you made: as long as nobody knows, you still have your job, your marriage, your reputation, your kids' opinion of you.

But look at what David actually says.

The silence was not protecting him. **The silence was costing him.**

It was taking his strength, day and night, in a way the thing itself had not.

A secret does not sit still. It grows, and it feeds on the energy you use to hold it down.

## Then One Line Changes

> "I acknowledged my sin to you. I didn't hide my iniquity. I said, I will confess my transgressions to Yahweh, and you forgave the iniquity of my sin." (Psalm 32:5)

Read how fast that happens.

He acknowledged. He stopped hiding. He said he would confess.

And before the sentence is even finished — *and you forgave*.

There is no waiting period. There is no probation. There is no "prove it first."

The forgiveness arrives inside the same sentence as the confession.

## Why This Is Hard Anyway

Telling God is one thing. He already knows, and most people half believe that nothing changes when they say it.

Telling a person is a different weight entirely.

And I am not going to pretend that is simple, or safe with everybody, or something you should do today just because a devotional said so.

Some people in your life would handle it badly. Some would use it. Some are not strong enough to carry it. That is a real thing and you are allowed to be careful.

But hear this clearly:

**A thing that nobody knows about cannot be helped by anybody.**

That is just the arithmetic of it. Secrets are where addictions are safest.

## Who To Tell

Not everybody. One person.

Somebody who meets three tests:

* 🤐 They can keep something to themselves
* 🧱 They are steady enough that this will not crush them
* ❤️ They want good for you more than they want to be shocked

That might be a friend. A pastor. A doctor. A counsellor. Somebody in a recovery group who has their own version of this and will not blink.

It does not have to be the person closest to you. Sometimes it should not be, at least not first.

## What To Watch For In Psalm 32:1-7

* 🎉 How the psalm opens before it gets heavy — he starts with "blessed"
* 🦴 What silence does to him physically in verses 3 and 4
* ⚡ How quickly forgiveness comes in verse 5
* 🏝️ What he calls God in verse 7, after it is out
* 🎵 The word "Selah" — a pause mark, a place to stop and let it land

## The Bigger Takeaway

You have been told that if people knew, you would lose everything.

What has actually happened is that keeping it secret has been quietly taking everything anyway. Your strength. Your sleep. Your nerve. The ease you used to have with people.

David found out that the moment it came out of his mouth, it started to weigh less.

**Not because the sin was smaller. Because he was no longer carrying it alone.**

## Today's One Thing

**Write one name.**

Just one. The person who could know and not destroy you with it.

You are not contacting them today. You are not confessing today. You are writing a name on a piece of paper.

If no name comes, that itself is important information, and it is worth saying plainly: your first step is probably not a conversation with a friend, it is a conversation with a professional — a doctor, a counsellor, or a recovery group where the entire point is that strangers can hear this without flinching.

If a name does come, look at it for a minute.

That is what the way out looks like from here.

## Today's Prayer

God,

I am so tired.

Not from work. From the managing. From keeping the two versions of me from meeting.

I did not realise how much of my strength was going into this until I stopped and counted it.

You say that when David stopped hiding, You forgave him in the same breath. I want to believe that is how You are with me.

So here it is. No editing. No softening.

And God, if there is a person who is meant to help carry this, show me who. Give me the nerve when the time comes.

I do not want to do the rest of my life in two halves.

In Jesus' name, amen.

day_title: What You Are Actually Thirsty For
reflection_question: What does the thing you reach for actually give you - calm, escape, confidence, numbness, company? Name the real need underneath it.
devotional_text:
Nobody gets addicted to a substance. Not really.

People get addicted to what it does for them.

So before we go any further, we have to ask a question that sounds simple and is not.

**What does it actually give you?**

Not what it costs. We will get to that. What does it *give*?

* 😮‍💨 Quiet, when your head will not stop
* 🛡️ Confidence you cannot find sober
* 🕳️ Numbness, when feeling it is unbearable
* 🏃 Escape from a situation you cannot fix
* 🫂 Company, when you are completely alone
* 🎁 A reward, in a life that does not give you many

That list is not an excuse. It is a diagnosis. And you cannot treat something you will not diagnose.

# A Woman At A Well

Jesus is sitting by a well in the middle of the day.

That detail matters. Nobody drew water at noon. You went in the cool of the morning, with the other women, together.

She came at noon because she was avoiding people.

Five husbands. Living with a man who was not her husband. A life that had become a thing people talked about.

She came when nobody else would be there, and somebody was there.

## He Asks Her For Water

That is how it starts. Not with a sermon. With Him needing something from her.

She is immediately defensive — He is a Jew, she is a Samaritan, this conversation should not be happening.

And then He turns it.

> "Everyone who drinks of this water will thirst again, but whoever drinks of the water that I will give him will never thirst again; but the water that I will give him will become in him a well of water springing up to eternal life." (John 4:13-14)

**Everyone who drinks of this water will thirst again.**

That is the most accurate description of addiction in the Bible.

It works. That is the problem. It genuinely works — for an hour, for an evening. And then the thirst comes back bigger, and the amount that used to be enough is not enough, and you need more of it more often just to get back to normal.

It is not that it fails you. It is that it never finishes.

## What He Does Not Do

He does not tell her to stop.

He does not list her failures and demand she clean up before He will talk to her.

He goes under it, to the thirst.

Because five husbands is not a marriage problem. Five husbands is somebody trying to get something out of a person that a person cannot give. She kept going back to the same well and it kept running dry.

Jesus is saying: you are not wrong to be thirsty. **You are drinking from something that cannot fill you.**

## He Does Not Avoid The Truth Either

He asks her to call her husband. She says she does not have one. He tells her the whole thing, plainly, without cruelty.

And she does not run.

That is remarkable. Somebody named the worst of her life out loud and she stayed.

She stayed because of *how* He said it. Nothing in His voice despised her.

**That is the thing to hold onto today. He can know the whole truth about you and still want the conversation.**

## What To Watch For In John 4:1-26

* 🕛 The time of day in verse 6, and why she came then
* 🙇 Who asks whom for help first
* 💧 The difference between water that runs out and water that springs up
* 🗣️ How Jesus brings up her life, and what He does not say about it
* 👑 Who He tells her He is, in verse 26 — and that He tells *her* first

## The Bigger Takeaway

The question is not "why am I so weak?"

The question is "what am I trying to get, and is there anywhere else to get it?"

Because the thirst underneath is often not a sinful thing at all. Wanting peace is not sinful. Wanting to feel safe, or wanted, or capable, or just quiet for twenty minutes — none of that is wrong.

You have been going to a well that charges you everything and leaves you thirsty by morning.

**Jesus is not offering you a dry life. He is offering you a full one.**

## Today's One Thing

**Finish this sentence honestly: "When I use, what I am really after is ______."**

Take your time with it. The first answer is usually not the real one.

"I want a drink" is not the answer. "I want to stop thinking about what happened" might be.

"I want to look at porn" is not the answer. "I want to feel wanted by somebody and nobody has looked at me like that in years" might be.

Get under it until you hit something that feels tender rather than shameful. That is usually where the truth is.

Then, and only then, ask the second question:

*Is there anywhere else I could get that?*

Do not solve it today. Just ask it.

## Today's Prayer

Jesus,

I know what I am thirsty for. I have just never said it out loud, because saying it makes me sound needy, and I would rather look like a man or a woman with a bad habit than one with a hole in them.

But You sat down with a woman everybody avoided and You did not flinch, and You did not start with her behaviour. You started with her thirst.

So start there with me.

Show me what I am actually reaching for.

And then show me whether You are really what You say You are, because I have been to this well a hundred times and I am always thirsty again by the morning.

I want the water that does not run out.

In Your name, amen.

reflection_question: How many times have you promised yourself you would stop? What did you rely on to make that promise work?
devotional_text:
Let us count something.

How many times have you decided to stop?

Not vaguely. Properly decided. Poured it away, deleted the app, blocked the number, told yourself this was the line.

Twice? Ten times? More than you can count?

And every single time, the plan was essentially the same.

**Try harder.**

Want it more. Mean it more. Be more disciplined than last time.

And here you are.

So today is not about trying harder. Today is about why that keeps failing, because until you understand that, you will just keep making the same promise with more feeling behind it.

# Willpower Is A Battery, Not A Generator

Willpower is real. It is just limited.

It runs down over a day. It runs down faster when you are tired, hungry, lonely, stressed or bored.

And here is the trap: **the thing you are fighting does not get tired.**

It waits. It is perfectly happy to wait until eleven at night when your battery is at four percent, because it only has to win once.

You have to win every single day. It has to win once a fortnight to stay alive.

That is not a fair fight, and losing it is not a character flaw. It is arithmetic.

## Paul Names The Problem

> "For the flesh lusts against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh; and these are contrary to one another, that you may not do the things that you desire." (Galatians 5:17)

That you may not do the things that you desire.

There is the gap again. The one Paul described in Romans 7 and the one you live in.

But look at what he says right before it.

> "But I say, walk by the Spirit, and you won't fulfill the lust of the flesh." (Galatians 5:16)

He does not say *fight the flesh harder*.

He says **walk by the Spirit**.

That is a completely different instruction, and most of us have never actually tried it. We have only ever tried the first one.

## What That Actually Means

It is not mystical. Watch the picture Paul uses a few verses later.

He talks about **fruit**.

> "But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faith, gentleness, and self-control. Against such things there is no law." (Galatians 5:22-23)

Notice where self-control is.

It is last on a list of *fruit*. Not first on a list of demands.

Fruit is not something a tree achieves by straining. Fruit is what grows out of a tree that is alive, planted somewhere good, and getting water.

So the question changes.

Not "how do I force self-control out of myself?"

But **"what am I rooted in, and what am I being fed?"**

## This Is Not Permission To Do Nothing

Be careful here, because there is a bad version of this.

The bad version says: effort is pointless, just let go and let God, and then nothing changes for another five years.

That is not what Paul means. He uses hard words in this same chapter — walk, crucify, keep step. Those are not passive.

The difference is not *effort* versus *no effort*.

The difference is **where the effort goes**.

Gritting your teeth at the moment of temptation is effort aimed at the last ten seconds, when you have already lost.

Building a life where you are fed, rested, honest, accountable and close to God is effort aimed at the whole day.

One of those is a battery. The other is being plugged in.

## What To Watch For In Galatians 5:13-26

* 🆓 What Paul says freedom is *for* in verse 13
* ⚔️ The two things at war in verse 17
* 📋 The list in verses 19 to 21, and how ordinary some of it is
* 🍇 That verse 22 calls it *fruit*, not achievements
* 👣 "Let's also walk by the Spirit" in verse 25 — walking, not sprinting

## The Bigger Takeaway

Every time you have failed, you have concluded something about yourself.

That you are weak. That you do not want it enough. That something is wrong with you specifically.

Consider another explanation.

**The method was wrong.**

You brought willpower to a fight willpower cannot win, over and over, and then blamed yourself for the result.

The next fifty-five days are about a different method. Not more straining. Different roots.

## Today's One Thing

**Find your low point in the day.**

Not the day of the week. The *hour*.

Think back over the last few months. When does it usually happen? What time is it? Where are you? What has just finished — work, the kids going to bed, a conversation that went badly?

Write down the hour.

That hour is where the fight actually is, and almost nobody plans for it. They plan for the big heroic moment and get ambushed by a Tuesday at 10 p.m.

For now, just know your hour. On Day 34 we will build something for it.

## Today's Prayer

God,

I have promised You I would stop more times than I can count.

I meant it every time. That is what frightens me.

I am starting to understand that I have been fighting this the wrong way — all teeth and no roots — and then hating myself when I ran out of strength at the end of a long day.

I do not fully understand what it means to walk by Your Spirit. I have mostly just tried to be good.

Teach me the difference.

Feed something in me that is stronger than what I am fighting, because what I have been running on is not enough and we both know it.

In Jesus' name, amen.
